title: KS-1372: retire the gateway's failed-login lockout (never fires), or wire it up?
bluf: Peter's ticket gives the two options and says 'whichever you prefer' (ticket description). Measured by the filer 2026-09-28: recordFailure is never called outside a unit test; slot 2's gateway logged 0 BRUTE_FORCE_LOCKOUT and 0 BRUTE_FORCE_BLOCKED over six hours with failed logins. Re-read in the local checkout a65ae7ed1: recordFailure appears only at middleware/security.ts:264 and in tests. Auth's own per-account lockout works (5 failures per email and /24, 15 minutes; ticket text) and you ruled it fail-closed on 2026-11-03 (card secuura-auth-lockout-failopen-redis-down-1103 = a). The gateway limiter is keyed per address and every caller shares one address on the demo (ticket, citing KS-618): wiring it could lock out every Stuart, Peter and demo user after one attacker's five failures (inference; UNMEASURED).

options.label: Retire it: delete the middleware, its config and the doc line
options.detail: A Secuura seat removes security.ts:146-192's lockout, config/services.ts bruteForce and the doc line, at tier 1. Auth's lockout stays the only one.

options.label: Wire it: call recordFailure/recordSuccess from the login response path
options.detail: A seat adds the calls plus a red-first test. Until KS-618 lands, it keys on a shared address (ticket).

options.label: Neither now
options.detail: Dead code stays; the ticket keeps its priority.

default_action: After 48 h: c. Nothing changes; Wednesday re-asks you. No seat touches the gateway.
